body:
Seems like we should use `HttpHeaderValues` here. The specification calls out the lowercase variant [1]. Should we change `HttpHeaderValues.UPGRADE` to lowercase, and should/are we using case insensitive compare when evaluating this header value?

[1] https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-6.7

> When Upgrade is sent, the sender MUST also send a Connection header
>    field (Section 6.1) that contains an "upgrade" connection option

We are using case-insensitive comparison, which is fine in my opinion. (more tolerating)

Jetty uses case-sensitive comparison and expects `Upgrade`, which seems incorrect. (They just do `.contains()` on a `List<String>` IIRC.)

So, we could:
- Use `HttpHeaderValues.UPGRADE` instead,
- Change it from `Upgrade` to `upgrade`, and
- Ping the Jetty folks about this so they fix this or they have a chance to disagree.

Here's the code that uses `.contains("Upgrade")`: 

https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/blob/65d33f8b49bd51140d9fe9b024c5dd42ad7571d8/jetty-server/src/main/java/org/eclipse/jetty/server/HttpChannelOverHttp.java#L373

`git blame` tells @gregw could help us here.
@trustin Ooops that looks wrong.  Fixing now..... standby.....

@trustin Thanks for confirming we use case-insensitive compare. I agree we should change `HttpHeaderValues.UPGRADE` to lowercase, and use it here.

@gregw - Thanks for the fix!
@trustin @Scottmitch   Fix is committed to jetty 9.3 and master branches: https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=483039
